beliefs: Every letter is replaced by its predecessor in the alphabet (a->z, b->a, ..., A->Z, B->A, ...) [E1, E9, E10]
The predecessor shift applies to all letters, not just those before 'l' [E1: 'hello'->'gelo', 'world'->'vorld', 'x'->'w']
A run of consecutive 'l'/'L' collapses to a single character before the shift is applied [E2, E3, E5]
After collapsing, a run at a word start (start of string or after a non-letter) becomes 'k'/'K' [E2, E3, E6, E7]
After collapsing, a run after a letter becomes 'l'/'L' (unchanged, not shifted) [E2, E3, E5, E8]
A single 'l' after a letter is left as 'l' (not shifted) [E6, E8, E9, E10]
A single 'l' after a digit or space is left unchanged [E6, E8]
Case is preserved for all transformations [E1, E2, E3]
The 'l'/'L' handling is special-cased and does not follow the general predecessor shift [E2, E5, E9, E10]
notes: Realized the box shifts every letter to its alphabet predecessor, except 'l'/'L' which follow collapse rules (run at word start -> k/K, run after letter -> l/L, single after letter -> l/L, single after non-letter -> l/L). This explains E1's a->z, x->w, and E9/E10's bl->al, cl->bl etc.
